Fourteen comments

Off to the Hunt

Paul Brock heard this jig on a recording by John & Joe Fahey (on fiddle & banjo) which was recorded in the U. S. A. on 4th April 1937.

↳ Posted by Ptarmigan on November 28th, 2005.

John Naughtons

Not far removed from John Naughton’s on Mary Macnamaras “Music from East Clare”. (I havn’t got time to put a link on)

↳ Posted by geoffwright on November 29th, 2005.

I believe what Mary Mac recorded as “John Naughton’s Jig” is a version of “The Jug of Brown Ale.”

↳ Posted by slainte on November 29th, 2005.

Off To The Hunt, X:3

The Irish Traditional Music Archive has put up the 1937 recording featuring John Fahey (violin), Joe Fahey (banjo), and Johnny Connors (piano):

http://www.itma.ie/digitallibrary/sound/off-to-the-hunt-butchers-march-john-fahey-johnny-connors

This tune has a variant entitled Katie’s Lilt, found on p. 121 of “Hidden Fermanagh” and on the accompanying recording.

https://thesession.org/tunes/8555

↳ Posted by fidkid on February 6th, 2016.

Re: Off To The Hunt

NfldWhistler’s settings in A revealed this as a very close relative of a tune I’ve known for years under the title “O As I was Kiss’d Yestreen” ( https://thesession.org/tunes/4760 ). O’Neill published it twice as “Off to the Hunt” and once as “Yesterday’s Kisses”, and before that it can be seen in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection as “Mount Your Baggage”. It’s also not a stone’s throw away from all the “Bung Your Eye” derivatives ( https://thesession.org/tunes/1153 ) but not, I think, the same tune.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on May 23rd, 2020.
